title: A Recipe for the Playlist
premise: Edmund Blackwood, a baker's daughter who channels her suppressed emotions into the bread she bakes, has survived three years at Hollow Creek High by being aggressively forgettable. But when her civics teacher pairs her with Theo Vance—her nemesis since freshman year—for a semester project on local history, they unearth a decades-old school board cover-up: a fire that closed the original Hollow Creek school, three students who were never accounted for, and hush money still flowing through town accounts. As Edmund and Theo dig deeper, someone starts sabotaging the bakery, threatening the only home she has. In the end, Edmund must choose between staying invisible to survive or testifying before the board with Theo beside her—and she discovers that love, like bread, only rises when you stop holding it down.
about_author: Mirabel Delacroix is a former small-town journalist who spent years covering school board meetings that nobody attended. She writes young adult fiction from a kitchen table perpetually dusted with flour.

chapters.title: The Bread Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet Edmund at 5 a.m. in Blackwood Bakery, kneading grief-sourdough for a classmate's canceled birthday party. Establishes her rule: bake the feeling, never show it. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Invisible Is a Skill
chapters.summary: Edmund navigates Hollow Creek High using her carefully mapped routes and seat choices, dodging attention—including Theo Vance, who mocks her in AP Civics. A pop quiz exposes that Edmund knows more about town history than she should. Beat: tension of a life built on avoidance.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Mr. Okafor announces semester-long paired projects on 'Hollow Creek: Then and Now'—and reads Edmund and Theo's names together. Both protest; he refuses to budge. Beat: dread, the collapse of Edmund's invisibility strategy.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Edmund and Theo negotiate a hostile truce over burnt coffee: split the work, zero contact beyond necessity. Theo reveals surprising knowledge of the old school site. Beat: grudging curiosity beneath antagonism.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Researching at home, Edmund finds her late grandmother's box: a 1989 newspaper clipping about the Hollow Creek Elementary fire, and a key labeled with an address that no longer exists. Beat: first crack in the family's silence.

chapters.title: The Address That Isn't
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo drives them to the address—a vacant lot behind the new municipal building. They argue, but Theo admits his uncle was a firefighter that night and never spoke again. Beat: reluctant alliance forming.

chapters.title: Three Names Missing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the county archive, the 1989 enrollment records have pages razored out. The librarian, Ms. Ferro, watches too long and slips Edmund a note: 'Ask about the scholarship fund.' Beat: the stakes sharpen.

chapters.title: Bread for a Funeral
chapters.summary: Edmund bakes memorial rolls for a beloved retired teacher's funeral and overhears board members whispering about 'the Vance kid asking questions.' Someone knows. Beat: fear arriving at her doorstep.

chapters.title: Truce Over Proofing Dough
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Theo shows up at the bakery uninvited; Edmund puts him to work shaping baguettes while they compare notes. Their rhythm in the kitchen surprises them both. Beat: warmth breaking through hostility.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Fund
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The 'Hollow Creek Futures Fund' receives $40,000 annually from the district—to a PO box. Cross-referencing, Edmund finds three names absent from every memorial: Priya Anand, Marcus Cole, and a third smudged beyond reading. Beat: cold horror.

chapters.title: Theo's Uncle Danny
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo visits his uncle's trailer; Danny, drunk and terrified, says only: 'They told us it was electrical. It wasn't.' He slams the door. Beat: guilt—Theo dragged family into danger.

chapters.title: Midterm Presentation
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Their interim presentation is polished and deliberately bland—but Mr. Okafor writes on their rubric: 'You're hiding the real story. I taught here in '89.' Beat: an unexpected ally, and vertigo.

chapters.title: Okafor's Confession
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Okafor, in his classroom after hours, admits he was a young teacher the night of the fire; he was paid off and transferred. He gives them a name: Superintendent Aldous Wren, then vice-principal, now board chair. Beat: the enemy gets a face.

chapters.title: Someone Was Here
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The bakery is ransacked overnight—nothing stolen except grandma's box. Dad assumes burglary; Edmund knows better. She bakes rage into rye until her knuckles bleed. Beat: violation, and resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Smudged Name
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Using yearbook photo forensics and a dental record request Theo's mom (a nurse) helps him navigate, they identify the third victim: Danny Vance's childhood best friend, Ruthie Okafor—the superintendent's own niece. Beat: devastating connection.

chapters.title: Wren Invites Them to Tea
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Superintendent Wren summons them, all charm and grandfatherly menace, offering glowing college letters in exchange for 'a focused, achievable project.' Edmund smiles and accepts. Beat: power showing its velvet glove.

chapters.title: Taking the Deal?
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Theo wants to take the letters—his family needs them. Edmund calls him a coward; he calls her reckless with other people's lives. They part furious. Beat: the alliance fractures under pressure.

chapters.title: Dad's Silence
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund confronts her father about grandma's box; he confesses grandma was the school secretary who kept the real enrollment ledger—and hid it before she died. He begs Edmund to let it stay buried. Beat: the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Following grandma's recipe annotations as a cipher, Edmund finds the ledger hidden inside the bakery's original brick oven wall. Three names, three dates, one line: 'Wren knew the doors were chained.' Beat: triumph curdling into terror.

chapters.title: Chained Doors
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The ledger proves the fire exits were chained shut during a lockdown drill gone wrong—and Wren ordered it. Theo photographs everything and sends copies to himself. Beat: evidence secured, paranoia rising.

chapters.title: Apology Bread
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund brings Theo a loaf scored with his name—an apology in her only fluent language. He eats it in silence, then says, 'We finish this together.' Beat: reconciliation, tenderness neither names yet.

chapters.title: Ms. Ferro's Warning
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The archivist warns them Wren has called in favors; her job is already gone. She hands over her private files and tells them to find Ruthie Okafor's mother. Beat: allies falling, torch passing.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Mother
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In a neighboring county, Ruthie's mother reveals Wren visited yearly—with an envelope—and that Ruthie didn't die in the fire. She survived, was placed with relatives, and died at nineteen. Beat: the cover-up deepens.

chapters.title: Not All Dead
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. If Ruthie survived, the death certificates are forged—which means criminal fraud, not just negligence. Theo realizes why his uncle drinks: he carried Ruthie out that night. Beat: hope and horror entwined.

chapters.title: The Fire That Follows
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A grease fire guts the bakery kitchen—arson, the inspector murmurs. Dad, burned and hospitalized, tells Edmund to stop. For the first time, she considers it. Beat: rock bottom.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund tries to quit: returns materials, emails Wren her withdrawal. Bakes nothing for three days. Theo waits outside her house every evening without knocking. Beat: grief, surrender, and the ache of unfinished truth.

chapters.title: Danny Talks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Danny, seeing the bakery burn on the news, breaks: he gives Theo his firefighter's logbook contradicting the official report, and agrees to testify. Beat: courage inherited from the broken.

chapters.title: The Loaf on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Theo leaves bread on Edmund's step—badly baked, lopsided, scored with her name. She laughs and cries at once, and understands: some things you can't carry alone. Beat: love admitted without saying it.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Case
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the hospital cafeteria, the pair rebuilds everything: ledger photos, Danny's logbook, Mrs. Okafor's envelopes, Ferro's files. Okafor offers to present it to the board himself. Beat: purpose rekindled.

chapters.title: Wren's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Wren has Okafor suspended pending 'investigation,' and the district attorney suddenly opens a case against Dad's bakery permits. Every lever of power turns at once. Beat: corruption flexing openly.

chapters.title: The Student Body Rises
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo leaks the story to the student paper; within days, lockers fill with photocopies of the three names. Students who never spoke to Edmund defend the bakery outside council chambers. Beat: solidarity, momentum.

chapters.title: Grandma's Recipe Box, Finished
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Deciphering the final cipher page, Edmund finds grandma's letter: she couldn't fight alone in 1989, and she's sorry. 'Finish the loaf,' it ends. Beat: inheritance of courage across generations.

chapters.title: Thirty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The board votes on Wren's new term Thursday. They have two days to get the evidence admissible, witnesses sworn, and the press in the room. A montage of sleepless preparation. Beat: ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund and Theo bake together through the night—not evidence, just bread, for the crowd they hope will come. Almost-kiss interrupted by a brick through the bakery window. Beat: intimacy shadowed by threat.

chapters.title: Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They present: ledger, logbook, forged certificates. Wren's lawyer moves to dismiss; the room erupts. Then Danny Vance walks in uniform and testifies. Beat: climax begins, voices shaking and steady.

chapters.title: Wren Breaks
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Confronted with Ruthie's survival and the yearly envelopes, Wren unravels on the record, blaming everyone but himself. The vote collapses; the state attorney general requests the file. Beat: power's public fall.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Okafor reinstated; Wren indicted; the bakery community-funded back to life. But three families grieve anew as the truth reopens old wounds. Beat: victory with weight.

chapters.title: Memorial Rolls
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the dedication of the Ruthie Anand Cole Memorial Garden, Edmund bakes three loaves—one for each name—and finally cries in public. Her father stands beside her. Beat: mourning made shared.

chapters.title: A Recipe for the Playlist
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Final project presented: not the safe history, but the true one, ending with a playlist of songs from 1989 that grandma left in the box. Okafor gives them an A and something like pride. Beat: full-circle closure.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (Actually)
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Epilogue: summer morning, bakery rebuilt, Theo's flour-dusted hands over hers on the dough. Edmund bakes joy for the first time without needing to hide anything else. Beat: love chosen over invisibility—warm, earned, done.
